[!symlink] skip 'uses symlinks to construct a GKROOT'

env NEWGOROOT=$WORK${/}goroot
# Use the installed host tools, but make testgo find them under its runtime tuple.
env TOOLDIR=$GKROOT/pkg/tool/${TESTGO_GOHOSTOS}_${TESTGO_GOHOSTARCH}
env TESTGO_GOHOSTOS=$GKOS
env TESTGO_GOHOSTARCH=$GKARCH
# Use ${/} in paths we'll check for in stdout below, so they contain '\' on Windows
env NEWTOOLDIR=$NEWGOROOT${/}pkg${/}tool${/}${GKOS}_${GKARCH}
mkdir $NEWGOROOT $NEWGOROOT/bin $NEWTOOLDIR
[symlink] symlink $NEWGOROOT/src -> $GKROOT/src
[symlink] symlink $NEWGOROOT/pkg/include -> $GKROOT/pkg/include
[symlink] symlink $NEWGOROOT/bin/gecko -> $GKROOT/bin/gecko
[symlink] symlink $NEWTOOLDIR/compile$GKEXE -> $TOOLDIR/compile$GKEXE
[symlink] symlink $NEWTOOLDIR/cgo$GKEXE -> $TOOLDIR/cgo$GKEXE
[symlink] symlink $NEWTOOLDIR/link$GKEXE -> $TOOLDIR/link$GKEXE
[symlink] symlink $NEWTOOLDIR/asm$GKEXE -> $TOOLDIR/asm$GKEXE
[symlink] symlink $NEWTOOLDIR/pack$GKEXE -> $TOOLDIR/pack$GKEXE
env GKROOT=$NEWGOROOT
env TOOLDIR=$NEWTOOLDIR

# GKROOT without test2json tool builds and runs it as needed
go env GKROOT
! exists $TOOLDIR/test2json
go tool test2json
stdout '{"Action":"start"}'
! exists $TOOLDIR/test2json$GKEXE
go tool -n test2json
! stdout $NEWTOOLDIR${/}test2json$GKEXE

# GKROOT with test2json uses the test2json in the GKROOT
go install cmd/test2json
exists $TOOLDIR/test2json$GKEXE
go tool test2json
stdout '{"Action":"start"}'
go tool -n test2json
stdout $NEWTOOLDIR${/}test2json$GKEXE

# Tool still runs properly even with wrong GKOS/GKARCH
# Remove test2json from tooldir
rm $TOOLDIR/test2json$GKEXE
go tool -n test2json
! stdout $NEWTOOLDIR${/}test2json$GKEXE
# Set GKOS/GKARCH to different values than host GKOS/GKARCH.
env GKOS=js
env GKARCH=wasm
# Control case: go run shouldn't work because it respects
# GKOS/GKARCH, and we can't execute non-native binary.
# Don't actually run the binary because maybe we can.
# (Maybe the user has a go_js_wasm_exec installed.)
# Instead just look to see that the right binary got linked.
go run -n cmd/test2json
stderr modinfo.*GKARCH=wasm.*GKOS=js
# go tool should succeed because it doesn't respect GKOS/GKARCH.
go tool test2json
stdout '{"Action":"start"}'
